Executive Order
UTAH
Under authority of the act of Congress approved June 25, 1910 (36 Stat . 847) ,
as amended by the act of August 24, 1912 (37 Stat . 497), it is hereby ordered that
the following described lands in the State of Utah be, and the same are hereby
temporarily withdrawn from settlement , location, sale or entry , except as provided
in said acts , for classification and in aid of proposed legislation :
Salt Lake Meridian
In T. 36 S. , R. 3 W. , unsurveyed land which will probably be when
surveyed Secs . 28 and 33 ;
In T. 37 S. , R. 3 W., Sec . 20 .
This order shall continue in full force and effect unless and until revoked by
the President or by act of Congress .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
December 14 , 1927.
[No. 4781 ]

Executive Order
It is hereby ordered that the several executive departments and independent
Government establishments in the District of Columbia , including the Government
Printing Office and the Navy Yard and Stations , be closed on Saturday , December
24, 1927 , and all clerks and other employees in the Federal service in the District
of Columbia , except those who may for special public reasons be excepted from the
provisions of this Order , or those whose absence from duty would be inconsistent
with the provisions of existing law, are hereby excused from duty on that day .
This Order is not to be deemed as establishing a precedent .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
December 16 , 1927 .
[No. 4782]

# machine location of an official printing (R37); not an authentication of the signed original


 
Executive Order
New Mexico
It is hereby ordered that Executive Order No. 4061 , dated August 12 , 1924,
withdrawing , among other lands, the public lands in Ts. 6 S. , Rs . 4 and 5 W., and
T. 7 S. , R. 4 W. , N. M. P. M., New Mexico , pending a resurvey , be and the same
is hereby revoked as to the above mentioned townships .
And it is hereby ordered , pursuant to Public Resolution No. 29 of February
14 , 1920 (41 Stat . 434), as amended January 21 and December 28, 1922 (42 Stat .
358 , 1067 ) , that the above described lands, subject to valid rights , shall be opened
only to entry under the homestead or desert land laws by qualified ex-service men
of the War with Germany , under the terms and conditions of such resolutions , and
the regulations issued thereunder , for a period of 91 days , beginning with the official
filing of the plat of resurvey and thereafter to appropriation under any public land
law applicable thereto , by the general public .
Subsequent to the date hereof , and prior to the date of restoration to general
disposition as herein provided, no right may be acquired to the released lands by
settlement in advance of entry, or otherwise , except strictly in accordance herewith .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
February 16 , 1928.
[No. 4811]
CA

Executive Order
MINNESOTA
It is hereby ordered , under authority of the act of Congress approved June 25,
1910 ( 36 Stat. 847), as amended by the act of August 24, 1912 (37 Stat . 497), that
the public lands exclusive of those in the Superior National Forest within the area
situated north of township 60 north in the counties of Cook , Lake and Saint Louis
in the State of Minnesota , including the natural shore lines of Lake Superior and
of the lakes and streams forming the international boundary in so far as they lie
within such area , be, and they are hereby temporarily withdrawn , subject to prior
claims under the public land laws legally initiated and maintained, for classification
and in aid of the legislation proposed in S. 3913 and H. R. 12780.
This order shall continue in full force and effect unless and until revoked by
the President or by act of Congress .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
May 26, 1928 .
[No. 4889]
CAL

Executive Order
Mr. John W. Addison , now serving in the excepted position of attorney and
examiner in the Federal Trade Commission, may be reinstated to his former competi￾tive classified status without regard to time limit on reinstatement under the civil
service rules .
Mr. Addison has had approximately seventeen years of Government service but
at the time of his appointment to his present excepted position he was not eligible for
reinstatement as a classified employee . When the rules were amended , June 25,
1921 , extending eligibility for reinstatement, in meritorious cases, one year for each
full year of service not exceeding five, he had been separated from his former
classified position for approximately five years and three months.
This order is recommended by the Federal Trade Commission in view of his long
and faithful service , which it is stated has been eminently satisfactory .
The Civil Service Commission concurs .
CALVIN COOLIDGE
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
December 15, 1928 .
[No.

Executive Order
1
Mr. Arthur J. Dahn may be reinstated as clerk in the Railway Mail Service
without regard to the time limit on reinstatement under the civil service rules .
Mr. Dahn was seriously injured in line of duty in a railroad wreck May 29 , 1918 .
As a result of this wreck he was incapacitated for service for several years .
This order is recommended by the Postmaster General . The Civil Service
Commission concurs .
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
January 19 , 1929 .

Executive Order
Mrs. Lee H. Garby , widow of Dr. Carl D. Garby , engaged in chemical work in
the Departments of Navy, War, and Agriculture from January 12, 1916 , to July 10 ,
1928 , may be appointed to an appropriate position in the classified service without
regard to the provisions of the civil service rules .
This order is recommended by the Secretary of Agriculture . The Civil Service
Commission is unable to concur .
For charity.
THE WHITE HOUSE ,
March 2 , 1929.
CALVIN COOLIDGE

Executive Order
Mr. George Henry Malone , yeoman, 1st class, U. S. Navy, may be appointed
to the position of supervising clerk , Office of the Captain of the Yard , Naval Sta￾tion , Cavite , P. I., to fill an existing vacancy , without regard to the Civil Service
Act or Rules .
This action is taken in view of the inability of the U. S. Civil Service Com￾mission to supply local American eligibles thru the Philippine Civil Service Bureau .
The Bureau of Navigation , Navy Department , will direct his discharge from the
Navy .

HERBERT
